criterion_notes.c1: Examines municipal domestic water (acueducto) and sewerage (alcantarillado) service access—specifically subscriber counts and municipal property coverage—across municipalities in Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda, Colombia.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording: YES — examines an administrative, institutional, and fiscal-governance instrument, namely municipal cadastral updating (actualización catastral under Art. 24 of Ley 1450 de 2011) and associated local fiscal capacity via property tax collection (impuesto predial) and intergovernmental transfers (SGP under Ley 1176 de 2007). Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: NO — does not examine a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements to obtain a utility connection, tariff or cost-recovery rules, discretion/accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure directly governing access). Instead, cadastral updating is analyzed as a macro-level municipal state-capacity and property-tax extraction tool to fund local public infrastructure and compute aggregate coverage denominators. Per A18, statistical significance or null findings play no role in this judgment.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary quantitative empirical analysis of longitudinal administrative datasets (IGAC, DNP, SSPD-SUI, INS) across up to 53 municipalities using robust paired-samples t-tests comparing 5-year pre- and post-update periods.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipal-level outcomes directly relevant to service access and connection: number of subscribers (suscriptores) and proxy service coverage (cobertura = subscribers divided by cadastral properties) for domestic water (acueducto) and sewerage (alcantarillado), alongside drinking-water quality risk (IRCA).
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the unit of analysis and sample (53 municipalities in Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda, with 33 municipalities analyzed for water and sewerage subscribers/coverage), exposure (year of municipal cadastral update), outcomes (property tax revenue, SGP transfers, water/sewerage subscribers and coverage, IRCA), and study design (quantitative before-and-after comparison over two 5-year windows using robust paired-samples t-tests).
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with English, Portuguese, Spanish, and French abstracts); translation/assessment from the provided Spanish full text is directly feasible per Criterion 10.

evidence_quotes.quote: This paper analyzes cadastral updating and its impact on the strengthening of local institutional capacities, from the point of view of property tax collection for the provision of home public utilities of water and sewerage.

¿Hay diferencias en el número de suscriptores de los servicios de acueducto y alcantarillado con la actualización del catastro? ¿Hay cambios en la cobertura de los servicios de acueducto y alcantarillado con la actualización catastral?

La unidad de análisis comprende los 53 municipios de los departamentos de Caldas, Quindío y Risaralda, como se muestra en la Figura 1; las observaciones se realizan en dos períodos que abarcan cinco años para cada periodo, divididos a partir del año de la actualización catastral.

En segundo lugar, en la variable impuesto predial, se observa que este mide la capacidad recaudatoria de un municipio y representa un probable aumento producto de la actualización catastral que determina los avalúos catastrales.

y aprovechar el potencial recaudatorio del predial es una condición necesaria que permitiría al municipio, en conjunto con el SGP, realizar las inversiones para construir y desplegar la infraestructura

raw_response.exposure: Municipal cadastral updating (actualización catastral; timing of municipal urban/rural property cadastre update) as a local institutional and fiscal-capacity instrument
raw_response.outcome: Municipal property tax collection (total and per capita), SGP drinking-water and sanitation intergovernmental transfers, water (acueducto) and sewerage (alcantarillado) subscriber counts and proxy coverage (subscribers per cadastral property), and Water Quality Risk Index (IRCA)
raw_response.population_and_sample: 53 municipalities in the departments of Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda, Colombia (33 municipalities analyzed for water and sewerage subscribers and coverage; 52 for SGP transfers; 42 for IRCA water quality), observed across two 5-year periods pre- and post-cadastral update within 2000-2020
raw_response.rationale: Exclude under E03 (Wrong exposure). The retrieved Spanish full text matches the record metadata (Pulgarín-Franco, 2024, DOI 10.15446/bitacora.v34n1.111741) and empirically evaluates municipal water (acueducto) and sewerage (alcantarillado) subscriber counts and coverage before and after municipal cadastral updating across Colombian municipalities (meeting c1, c3, c4, c5, and c6). However, under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, the exposure—periodic municipal cadastral updating examined as a local state-capacity and property-tax revenue extraction tool (impuesto predial) alongside intergovernmental transfers (SGP) to finance public infrastructure—is a municipal public-finance/macro-capacity factor rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as tenure/documentation prerequisites for utility connection, eligibility screening, tariff/cost-recovery rules, enforcement, or utility regulatory structure). Statistical significance of reported results played no part in this decision.
raw_response.study_design: Quantitative before-and-after municipal comparison using robust paired-samples t-tests across 5-year pre- and post-cadastral-update periods
